diagnostic.question: Can you explain the main purpose of spread and rest before reading?
diagnostic.answer: A complete answer should name the problem it solves, the values or control flow involved, and one mistake to avoid.

sections.title: The same dots have two jobs
sections.body: Spread expands an iterable or object into another literal or call. Rest collects remaining arguments or pattern values into one array or object. Read the surrounding syntax: on the input side it collects; in an array, object, or call it expands.

sections.title: Array spread
sections.body: [...items] creates a shallow array copy, and [...left, ...right] combines arrays. The outer array is new, but nested objects keep the same references. Spread is useful for immutable updates such as [...items, newItem], but repeated spreading of huge arrays can cost time and memory.

sections.title: Object spread
sections.body: { ...user, name: "Mina" } copies enumerable own properties and then replaces name. Later properties win. It is a shallow copy, so nested objects are shared unless you copy the specific nested level too. Getters and special descriptors are not preserved like a full clone.

sections.title: Rest parameters
sections.body: function sum(...numbers) collects supplied arguments into a real array. A rest parameter must be last and there can be only one. Prefer a clear array or options object when an unbounded argument list would make the API harder to understand.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Spread and rest is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you prove that code using spread and rest behaves correctly?
interviewQuestions.answer: State the expected value or control flow first, test normal and boundary cases, and inspect the actual runtime result. Explain the JavaScript rule behind the evidence.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which edge case would you test first?

interviewQuestions.question: Where can spread and rest affect React code?
interviewQuestions.answer: It can affect values, callbacks, rendering decisions, updates, or data flow. The exact connection depends on the concept; the important step is to reason from JavaScript behavior before blaming React.

commonMistakes.symptom: Code using spread and rest produces a surprising value.
commonMistakes.cause: The result was run before the value, type, scope, identity, or control flow was predicted.
commonMistakes.fix: Reduce the case, write the expected result, and apply the exact rule from the matching section.

commonMistakes.symptom: A learner copies syntax but cannot adapt it.
commonMistakes.cause: The example was memorized without explaining why it works.
commonMistakes.fix: Change the data and names, predict again, and explain which behavior must stay the same.

commonMistakes.symptom: A React problem is blamed on React immediately.
commonMistakes.cause: The underlying JavaScript behavior was not isolated first.
commonMistakes.fix: Reproduce the value or function behavior in a small JavaScript example, then reconnect it to the component.
